newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Oct 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Oct 7.

text.p: The following is a summary of major Indonesian political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Jakarta. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (6221) 384-6364. Fax: (6221) 344-8404.
Iwa Sewaka, president director of state-owned satellite operator PT Satelindo, said that the company will float shares on the Jakarta bourse in 1998.

Indonesian Armed Forces Commander General Feisal Tanjung said that the national police should play a greater role in internal security matters. The comments came after President Suharto, speaking at the 51st anniversary of the Indonesian armed forces, on Saturday, said that the police, and not the army, should be used to tackle internal security problems.
Indonesia's plywood exports to Japan rose by 11 percent in the first nine months of 1996.

President Suharto is likely to broach the subject of the disputed Sipadan and Ligitan islands during his talks with Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad. Diplomatic sources said the subject was likely to be on the agenda despite comments last week by Mahatir to the contrary.

The Indonesian navy has caught a further 24 foreign ships illegally fishing in the waters of eastern Indonesia, Navy Chief Admiral Arief Kushariadi said on Saturday. The boats, from Thailand and Taiwan, had a combined crew of around 300.
Indonesian cigarette giant PT Sampoerna said it had secured loans of US$400 million for business expansion.
